_about: The one source of facts about Mark for agents: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, the structured data (JSON-LD) on every page and the homepage's copy of it are all built from this file. Every line here is already published on the homepage; change the homepage and this file together. Never add a fact Mark has not approved.
name: Mark Hallam
positioning: Solving hard problems from first principles and shipping with agents.
summary: I solve hard problems and make things that work in the real world. Most of my career has been in aviation: bringing ten Airbus A320s into Australia, writing the maintenance manuals a new airline started flying with, and getting a hydrogen drone program up and flying. Now I work out the problem from first principles and get AI agents to build it.
about: I'm not a developer. My background is aerospace and aviation, and in every role the job was the same: find where a complicated system isn't working, work out what's actually true, and fix the cause.

Now I use the same method with AI. I strip a problem back to what's actually true, write it down so clearly that an agent can't misread it, then let a team of AI agents build it while I check the results like an engineer would. I'm writing up what I learn as I go, from Melbourne.
contact: Get in touch about roles and projects building with, or for, AI agents.

builds.name: LVLme
builds.summary: Free, open source software that helps you land the job you want. It works with the AI you already use, such as Claude, Codex or Cursor, and runs on your own computer, so your information stays private.

builds.name: mStack
builds.summary: My open source collection of skills: reusable instructions that work with whichever AI agent you already use, built for people and agents alike. The first is the design review loop I run on this site: two AI reviewers from different makers score every journey out of 10, I fix what they find, and we repeat until both give it 10. An outcome-first skill for autonomous work is next.

builds.name: SKYCOT
builds.summary: A Mac app where kids describe the app they want and AI builds it, with a parent in the loop. 39 beta builds in eight days.

builds.name: Argo
builds.status: Retired in June 2026; code private; figures self-reported
builds.summary: A platform for AI teammates, with permissions, approvals and a tamper-evident audit trail. A swarm of AI coding agents built it around the clock under my direction: 2,901 pull requests merged in eight weeks. Retired in June 2026; its lessons went into SKYCOT.

builds.name: My agent job board
builds.summary: I post jobs on GitHub and Claude and Codex pick them up, do the work, ask me when something is unclear, and report back done or blocked. My first board closed 95 jobs across three computers in eight days.

builds.name: DAC (Declarative Agent Compilation)
builds.summary: An open-source prompt compiler, MIT licensed, that turns a plain-English idea into a plan many agents can run in parallel. It started life as GYSOM.

builds.name: AI Insider Threat Test
builds.summary: A toolkit that checks whether a business's AI assistant stays inside its agreed limits: 23 tests on what it can read, what it can do without approval, and whether it stops when told. Built in September 2026; not yet run with a real client.

builds.name: AI Beyond Alignment
builds.summary: An independent research record asking whether behavioural alignment is enough to keep highly capable autonomous AI safe. 139 claims checked against 219 sources over 33 audit rounds, including an adversarial review that withdrew two of my own claims. Paused in September 2026; no paper yet.

hardProblems.title: Bringing ten A320s into Australia.
hardProblems.story: Every aircraft needed regulator approvals, paperwork and a delivery slot before it could carry a passenger. I held all three, through to the airline's last A320 in 2014.

hardProblems.title: Writing the rules a new airline flew by.
hardProblems.story: When Tigerair Australia started up, I wrote its maintenance documents, including the aircraft maintenance schedule, minimum equipment list and configuration deviation list.

hardProblems.title: A maintenance base from a blank page.
hardProblems.story: Took the Adelaide line maintenance base from tender to regulator approval, doubling the maintenance ports in the network.

hardProblems.title: Finding fuel in the engines.
hardProblems.story: An engine wash program recovered 2 to 3 percent engine performance and saved more than $500,000 a year in fuel.

hardProblems.title: Moving every maintenance record without losing one.
hardProblems.story: Migrated the fleet's maintenance data from SIA Engineering's SAP system to Air New Zealand: the records that prove every aircraft is safe to fly.

hardProblems.title: Phones on, gate to gate.
hardProblems.story: Ran the program that won CASA approval for passengers to use their devices from boarding to arrival.

hardProblems.title: New rules for twin-engine jets.
hardProblems.story: Moved the fleet onto CASA's new extended diversion time rules (EDTO), which set how far a two-engine jet may fly from a suitable airport.

hardProblems.title: Selling through COVID.
hardProblems.story: My best sales month came in May 2020, at 133 percent of the year before.

hardProblems.title: Australia's first hydrogen drone, cleared for takeoff.
hardProblems.story: Set up the university's drone operator's certificate and was the person accountable to CASA for it. Worked through the rules for carrying hydrogen gas, and held the schedule and budget for Hydrogen to the Skies.

hardProblems.title: Enabling the benefits of CMATS, Australia's new air traffic system.
hardProblems.story: My part at Airservices Australia is making the benefits of CMATS, Australia's new air traffic system, real for the people who fly.

career.role: Project Manager (Engineering), Deputy Quality Manager, Executive Engineer
career.detail: Ten and a half years. Entry into service of ten A320s, through to the airline's last in 2014; the move to the new EDTO rules, gate-to-gate device approval, the digital maintenance records program, and the 2015 migration of maintenance data to Air New Zealand. Ran the engineering audit program as Deputy Quality Manager. As Executive Engineer, wrote the start-up maintenance documents, ran the regulator approvals and paperwork for new A320 deliveries, set up the Adelaide maintenance base, introduced the engine wash program, contracted ground support equipment across the network, and recovered more than $1 million in hail damage insurance claims.
